header:
What a stock split
really does

lines.text: In April 2026, Booking turned one share worth over $4,000 into 25.
lines.say: Booking turned one share worth over four thousand dollars into twenty-five.

lines.text: Owners got 24 extra shares for every share. Nobody got a dollar richer.
lines.say: Owners got twenty-four extra shares for every share, and nobody got a dollar richer.

lines.text: A split gives you more shares, but each one is worth less, so your total stays the same.
lines.say: A split gives you more shares, but each one is worth less, so your total stays the same.

lines.text: For example, one $4,000 share becomes 25 shares at $160. Still $4,000.
lines.say: For example, one four-thousand-dollar share becomes twenty-five shares at a hundred sixty dollars. Still four thousand.

lines.text: Booking had about 775 million shares as of April 20, 2026. Same pizza, more slices.
lines.say: Booking itself had about seven hundred seventy-five million shares after the split. Same pizza, more slices.

lines.text: So why bother? The SEC says companies often split to make shares more affordable.
lines.say: So why bother? The SEC says companies often split to make shares more affordable.

lines.text: Here's the surprise: Nvidia has split six times since 2000. One share from 1999 is now 480.
lines.say: Here's the surprise. Nvidia has split six times since two thousand, so one share from nineteen ninety-nine is now four hundred eighty.

lines.text: But those splits added nothing. Each one cut the price by the same amount. The growing business did the work.
lines.say: But those splits added nothing, because each one cut the price by the same amount. The growing business did the work.

lines.text: A split changes the price tag, not what you own.

post.title: Booking turned 1 share into 25. Nobody got richer.
post.ig:
Booking turned one share worth over $4,000 into 25. Nobody got richer.

A stock split gives you more shares, each worth less. Your total stays the same.
Example: 1 share at $4,000 = 25 shares at $160 = still $4,000.
Booking's 25-for-1 split took effect in April 2026.
One Nvidia share from 1999 is 480 shares after six splits, but the splits added $0. The business growth did the work.

Sources: SEC, Booking Holdings 8-K and 10-Q (2026), Nvidia 8-K (2024).
